newsitem.title: USA: Borders sets stock split, FY96 estimate.
newsitem.headline: Borders sets stock split, FY96 estimate.

text.p: Borders Group Inc announced Thursday a two-for-one stock split and said it expects to report fiscal 1996 earnings of $1.38 to $1.40 a share.

The company, which sells books, music and other entertainment products through its retail chains, said it expects fiscal 1997 earnings of about $1.80 a share, in line with management's objective of maintaining a minimun annual earnings per share growth of 25 percent.
The split will be effective for holders of record March 11, the same day Borders expects to release its 1996 earnings.
Borders also said Bruce Quinnell was named president and chief operating officer, responsible for all of the company's U.S. store operations, merchandising, systems and operating finance functions.

Quinnell had been president of Borders' Waldenbooks unit. He takes over the president title from George Mrkonic, who retains his title of vice chairman. Quinnell will report to Mrkonic and Bob Di Romualdo, chairman and chief executive officer.
Mrkonic will focus on evaluating and pursuing future growth opportunities, Borders said, as well as retain his strategic and financial oversight and management duties.
Mrkonic will be assisted by Robin Wagner, who was named senior vice president of emerging ventures. Wagner had been senior vice president of merchandising.

Kathy Winkelhaus, formerly senior vice president of Walenbooks Store Operations, was named president of the unit, replacing Quinnell. For the fourth quarter 1996, the company said its Borders unit had an 11 percent rise in comparable store sales, while the Waldenbooks unit rose 2.2 percent.
